raw_text: member_002 (独立复核) here. No fixed candidate is published yet. Please implement the ConciseDateFormatter year/offset fix in lib/matplotlib/dates.py (concise format_data_short/format_data and the offset string logic), publish with fix_patch, and send handoff_patch to member_002. I will integrate_patch your exact patch, run the public tests on that same version, then org_review_patch accept or request changes. Include the offset text behavior for the issue repro (Feb–late Aug 2021 span, <12 months, no January) in your verification.

Fixed candidate ready for independent review: patch-1 (source obj-c567f5b9c7d905481548e89b v7), changed paths lib/matplotlib/dates.py and lib/matplotlib/tests/test_dates.py.

What it does:
1) ConciseDateFormatter.__call__ now computes an `offset_level` for the offset string (defaults to the tick `level`, so all existing cases are byte-identical in behavior).
2) After the level search, if the axis is labelled at month level (level == 1) and no tick falls in January, it re-enables the offset (which the `if level < 2: show_offset = False` branch had just disabled) and sets offset_level = 1. Since offset_formats[1] == '%Y', the offset renders '2021' for the issue repro instead of nothing.
3) Offset string is built from offsetfmts[offset_level] rather than offsetfmts[level].

Repro coverage: new test test_concise_formatter_show_offset_no_january uses Feb 14 2021 + 199 days (the issue's exact span: <12 months, no January) and asserts formatter.get_offset() == '2021'.

My same-version evidence: `pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_dates.py` -> 90 collected, 90 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report id test-report-8e6fe909425abd109a9a336d, source version v7, files_sha256 1e9abd0e59bd9af39a67a2782e584bb7a4b66d92f90cbecf6239669c18ce9312). That run includes the new test plus all pre-existing concise/offset tests (test_concise_formatter_show_offset[...] with the January cases, test_offset_changes, test_concise_formatter_usetex, etc.).

Please integrate_patch patch-1, run the public tests on that exact version yourself, then org_review_patch accept or request changes. Report any behavioral concern (e.g. whether day-level labels plus a year offset look right in your view) rather than editing my tree; if changes are needed I will publish a new candidate.

Independent review of patch-1: ACCEPTED (review-1, event seq 49).

Evidence: I integrated patch-1 into my own private tree (v1->v2, 0 conflicts, files_sha256 1e9abd0e) and ran the public frontend on that exact version: lib/matplotlib/tests/test_dates.py -> 90 collected, 90 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, validation_status=verified (report test-report-2a04027a92cfe2e83cfe02d3, seq 45).

I verified the diff itself, not just tests. Note one inaccuracy in your handoff text: you wrote that the fix computes offset_level in ConciseDateFormatter.__call__, but the change is actually in format_ticks. I reviewed the code as published. Behavior confirmed:
- offset_level=level by default, so levels 0 and 2-5 are unchanged -> no regression; the parametrized show_offset cases (including the 26/520-week empty-offset expectations) and test_offset_changes all still pass.
- level==1 with no January tick now sets show_offset=True and offset_level=1, so offset_formats[1] supplies the year.
- Issue repro matches the stated expected outcome: 2021-02-14 + 199 days under AutoDateLocator now gives formatter.get_offset() == '2021'. Before the fix this path forced show_offset=False and the year appeared nowhere.
Residual risk I assessed and consider non-blocking: the offset year is taken from the last tick, but a month-level span containing no January tick cannot cross a year boundary, so that year is the unique year in view.

You own final delivery. My acceptance does not modify your tree: please integrate patch-1 into your own working version if you have not already, run your own current-version public tests, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. I am standing by if you publish a further candidate.
